question:
In the classical Rutherford model, an electron (mass $m$, charge magnitude $e$) is assumed to revolve in a circular orbit of radius $r$ around a proton (charge $+e$) due to electrostatic attraction.

Assume the electrostatic force magnitude is $F=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{e^2}{r^2}$ and the orbit is circular with speed $v$, so that the centripetal condition is $\dfrac{mv^2}{r}=F$. The centripetal acceleration is $a=\dfrac{v^2}{r}$.

Classical electrodynamics predicts that an accelerating charge radiates energy. For this question, take the radiated power to be $P=\alpha a^2$, where $\alpha$ is a positive constant.

Evaluate the stability of the Rutherford atom by answering the following:

(i) Derive how $a$ and hence $P$ depend on $r$ (core derivation).

(ii) Using the given potential energy $U(r)=-\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{e^2}{r}$ and kinetic energy $K=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$, obtain the total energy $E(r)=K+U$ (core derivation).

(iii) Since radiation implies $\dfrac{dE}{dt}=-P$, infer how $E$ and $r$ change with time and conclude whether the classical atom is stable (application/inference).

(iv) If the orbital radius decreases from $r_0$ to $\dfrac{r_0}{2}$, compare the radiated power in the two situations and comment on how the tendency to collapse changes.

options.A: $E$ decreases (becomes more negative) and $r$ decreases; as $r$ decreases the radiation increases as $P\propto \dfrac{1}{r^4}$, so the electron spirals into the nucleus (unstable).
options.B: $E$ increases (becomes less negative) and $r$ increases; as $r$ increases the radiation increases as $P\propto r^4$, so the electron spirals away (stable).
options.C: $E$ remains constant but the orbit becomes elliptical; radiation changes only the shape, not the size of the orbit.
options.D: $E$ decreases but $r$ remains constant because angular momentum is conserved, so the electron keeps orbiting at the same radius.
